classification.difficultyReason: The task is scaffolded in three steps. Part a reads the overlap side from the diagram, since the overlap is a square and so equals the 5 cm width. Part b is a single subtraction, 12 - 5 = 7. Part c adds only the outside edges of the L-shape, so the student must identify which edges are exposed and leave out the internal seam. This is more than p12-q4, which is a direct unit conversion and a rectangle perimeter. It needs a little more spatial interpretation than that. It is easier than p14-q9, the same context unscaffolded at 65, because the sub-questions supply the key decisions. The only real demand is interpreting the overlap diagram and choosing the outer edges, which is about the same as p7-q7's two-step conversion and division.

content.prompt: Two identical rectangles of card, each $12\text{ cm}$ by $5\text{ cm}$, overlap in a square to make the shape shown.

children.label: a
children.prompt: What is the side length of the overlap?

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the length of each exposed inner edge.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the perimeter of the new shape.

answer.worked:
Add only the outside edges.
$$\begin{align*}P&=12+5+7+7+5+12\\P&=48\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
